sections.name: goal
sections.value: Build PRD 003's seat messaging permissions, and who may designate the prime. Caller identity rests on what the daemon already knows (ruling C33), not on per-seat credentials.

value.title: Seat identity provenance: route inventory, capability bootstrap, then gated routes
value.done_when: Every route the checked route inventory lists as seat-authority refuses a caller that holds the daemon key but not the incarnation capability of the seat it claims to act as (the claimed caller's, not each operation's subject), with a regression per route class; the inventory sensor passes at the shipping head. Plan 221 is phase 1 (the inventory sensor and the capability-bootstrap workshop); later phases are planned from the workshop.
value.note: Abandoned by ruling C33 (2026-11-09): req-10 is dropped, plan 223 stopped and #183 closed unmerged. Plan 221 (phase 1, shipped) stays: its route-inventory sensor is kept, and workshop 001 stays on file for a future shared or multi-user host.

value.title: Only the recorded prime, the operator or an audited --force sets or retires the prime
value.done_when: A seat that isn't the recorded prime is refused set and retire with nothing written; the recorded prime and an audited --force succeed; a self-designation attempt is refused; every set and retire writes one spine event with the actor and reason.
value.note: Independent of s01 (req-10): it needs authority over the designation, not caller proof, so it may run in parallel. Its tests keep the unforced refusals separate from the operator and audited --force paths (review of #112).

value.title: A seat's messaging policy: open by default, can be locked down, changed by its parent or prime
value.done_when: A new seat can message any seat; a seat locked to a set can message only that set; its parent or the prime changes the policy, anyone else (and the seat itself) needs --force with a reason, audited. The policy is outbound only (q-02).

value.title: The daemon enforces it: parent and prime reachable, actionable refusals, senders told, replies and outputs included, no new cost
value.done_when: A locked-down seat always reaches its parent and its community prime, else any prime on the machine (q-03), and the operator and the Telegram bridge, for identities the daemon derives, never claimed (q-04, C33); a refused send names the policy and the way to get it changed, and --force sends it anyway, audited (q-02); a sender learns when the recipient can't reply to it; replies and outputs follow the same rule; the cost backpressure row shows no new per-tick or per-seat launch.

value.title: Roles carry a default messaging policy
value.done_when: Assigning a role whose definition carries a default policy applies it to the holder's seat, and releasing the holding restores the seat's own policy.

value.change: Created with PRD 003 (#112) so the coverage sensor sees every requirement delivered by a planned step. req-10 first (plan 221); the permission steps wait on Jordan's q-02 to q-04. Owner pm-001 until the prime gives it a PM of its own.
s01 in progress under plan 221 (docs/plans/221-seat-provenance): phase 1 ships the route inventory and its sensor and the capability bootstrap workshop; the gated routes follow in phase 2.

PRD 003 q-02 to q-04 answered, so s03 to s05 no longer wait on them and stay planned (not started). s01 stays in progress (plan 223, phase 2 of req-10). s02 is independent of s01. s01 done_when: the capability is the claimed caller's (review of #112).

Ruling C33: s01 abandoned (req-10 dropped, plan 223 stopped, #183 closed); plan 221's route-inventory sensor and workshop 001 stay. s03 no longer depends on s01; s04's exemption rests on identities the daemon derives. The goal no longer puts caller proof first.
